newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises along with natgas futures.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises along with natgas futures.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Tuesday in line with a sharp rise in natural gas futures, industry sources said.
"(Electricity futures) are in a bit of a sideways market but there is some upward pressure because of gas futures," said one New York-based futures broker.
Gas futures were surging Tuesday, with December Henry Hub up 14.2 cents to $3.12 per million British thermal units as of 1230 EST.
Also as of 1230 EST, December California Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures were trading up 39 cents at $26.30 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $27.00 per MWh.
January COB was bid at $23.05 and offered at $23.50 after trading steady from Monday's close at $23.00 per MWh.
December Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 60 cents at $24.60 after reaching as high as $25.25 per MWh, while January PV was up 67 cents at $22.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1210 EST a total of 37 COB and 47 PV contracts had traded.
